name: block-route-card
use: How a request, a payment or a visitor moves through the product: two to five stations, each with an icon, a name and what it does, and a note for the way back.
avoid: Steps the reader must take in order (take block-flow); more than five stations.
props: { kind: 'block-route-card'; title: string; stations: { name: string; text: string; icon?: 'user' | 'key' | 'app' | 'store' | 'plug' | 'card' | 'bank' | 'check' | 'mail' | 'globe' }[]; note?: string; noteDirection?: 'back' | 'forward' }

cases.title: How a payment goes from an element to the Stripe account
cases.why: Four stations make the hidden path of the money visible.

props.title: How a payment goes

stations.name: Your element
stations.text: Asks for a payment link: the amount, the currency and its own order number.

stations.name: Stripe element
stations.text: Creates a Stripe Checkout session with your keys and returns its link.

stations.name: Stripe Checkout
stations.text: Takes the card on the side of Stripe; card numbers never pass through your computer.

stations.name: Your Stripe account
stations.text: Receives the money at the prices of Stripe.

props.note: Stripe then sends a signed event back, and the element records it for the element that sold.

cases.title: How a visitor gets into an application
cases.why: Three stations show which service checks what.

props.title: How a visitor gets in

stations.name: Visitor
stations.text: Signs in with a password, Google, a magic link or an email address as a guest.

stations.name: Sign-in service
stations.text: Checks the account and its roles, then starts the session.

stations.name: Application
stations.text: Opens the pages the role allows.

props.note: Each application keeps its own accounts.

docs: npx shadcn add @fractera/block-route-card. On a page by itself or as the figure of block-hero-figure: { "kind": "block-route-card", "title": "…", "stations": [ { "name", "text", "icon" } ], "note": "…" }.
